data.name: Mizan
data.gender_notes: Mizan is used as a male name in Islamic naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Mizan is a Quranic name derived from the Arabic word 'mizan', meaning a balance or a scale. It refers to the concept of justice and fairness that is weighed against good deeds and bad deeds on the Day of Judgment. The name Mizan carries the meaning “Justice, Balance” and is chosen by families in Islamic traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Arabic tradition and is also used in Arabic, Urdu, Persian. Parents who choose Mizan usually hope their child will grow to embody justice, balance and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: A name symbolizing the quest for balance and justice in life.
data.etymology: Mizan belongs to the Arabic linguistic tradition and is used in Islamic naming. Its recorded meaning is “Justice, Balance.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Mizan total 9, giving a life-path number of 9. Number 9 is linked with Mars and with the qualities of compassion, idealism and generosity.

Mizan was a title used by the Abbasid Caliphs to denote their role as chief justices and maintainers of the scales of justice.
Time period: 750-1258 AD
Context: The Abbasid Caliphate was the successor state to the Umayyad Caliphate and is considered the golden age of Islamic civilization.

Mizan is also the name of a constellation in Ursa Minor, known as the 'Balance' or 'Scales'.
Time period: Pre-Islamic era
Context: In Islamic astronomy, this constellation is considered one of the 28 constellations mentioned in the Quran.
